item.title: Under-Bed Storage Containers: Choose by Clearance, Access, and Dust
item.description: Under-bed storage can add capacity without taking another inch of visible floor, but only when the container fits the bed and can be pulled out without disturbing the room. The common mistake is measuring the open gap once, buying a bin that matches that number and discovering that the frame, the rug, the wheels or the lid make it too tall. This guide measures the lowest point, adds up the container’s full height, checks the pull-out route and then assigns each box a single job.

item.title: Small Bedroom Storage That Keeps a Clear 30-by-48-Inch Space Beside the Bed
item.description: Most bedroom storage advice starts under the bed. In a small bedroom, the thing that decides whether the room works is the floor beside it: room to step out of bed, make the bed and open a drawer without turning sideways. A useful benchmark is the clear floor space defined in the ADA Standards, at least 30 inches by 48 inches, which they require beside beds in guest rooms with mobility features.
